examples.knowledge_point: Integrating Using the Squared Cosine Variant of the Cosine Double-Angle Formula
examples.worked_solution:
Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the $\cos^2{x}$ term, given by

$$
\cos{2x} =2\cos^2 x -1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
\cos^2 x = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\cos 2x +1 \right).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\eqalign{
		\int \cos^2 x \, \textrm{d}x&=\int  \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\cos 2x +1 \right) \, \textrm{d}x\[5pt]
								&=\dfrac{1}{2}\int ( \cos {2x} +1) \textrm{d}x\[5pt]
                                                                 &= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\sin {2x} +x\right) + C\[5pt]
								&= \dfrac{1}{4}\sin {2x} +\dfrac{1}{2}x + C.
								
	}
$$

Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve $y=3{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})-3{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})+2x+1,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=\pi ,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The area of the region is given by

$$
A={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(3{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})-3{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})+2x+1)\,\text{d}x.
$$

To calculate this integral, we use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x={cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

We can rewrite the above formula as

$$
3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=3{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})-3{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2}).
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(3{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})-3{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})+2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(3\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+{x}^{2}+x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =[3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+(\pi )^{2}+\pi ]-[3\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+(0)^{2}+0] \\  & =[0+{\pi }^{2}+\pi ]-0 \\  & ={\pi }^{2}+\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
